spells.name: Aid

fields.Materials: White cloth strip with sticky ends; holy symbol

effect: Grants the benefit of bless and 1d8 temporary hit points, which can raise the recipient above normal maximum hp.
Damage removes these extra hp before regular hp.
conditions: Both benefits end with the spell.
exceptions: Curative magic cannot restore temporary hp already lost.

spells.name: Detect Life
effect: Determines whether a creature is alive, including plants and bodies in feigned death, suspended animation, coma or astral travel.
conditions: Finds the first living creature on the caster’s line of sight, or the first to cross that line during the duration.
If more than one inch of wood or stone intervenes, each inch reduces the range as 10 feet of open space.
exceptions: Metal barriers of any thickness defeat the spell.
Mental protection, whether psionic or magical, also prevents detection.

spells.name: Holy Symbol

fields.Materials: An appropriately crafted religious symbol; not consumed

effect: Prepares a cleric’s holy symbol, including a replacement or spare.
conditions: Its material and design must suit the caster’s own deity or religion.
A cleric can possess two holy symbols at once.
exceptions: The symbol is not itself a magic item; a good or evil cleric’s symbol has a faint corresponding aura, while a morally neutral cleric’s has none.

spells.name: Wyvern Watch

fields.Materials: Holy or unholy symbol

effect: Creates a hazy guard that attacks a creature approaching within 1″.
A failed spell save paralyzes the intruder for 1 round/caster level.
conditions: A successful save leaves the guard active; its first successful strike expends it.
The haze is detectable with 90% probability in bright light, 30% in twilight, and 0% in darkness.
exceptions: The caster can release the victim; dispel magic or remove paralysis also frees it.

spells.name: Detect Poison

fields.Area: About 1 cubic yard scanned per round
fields.Materials: Mistletoe and yew leaves

effect: Detects poison in a scanned object, creature or portion of an area.
There is a 5% chance per caster level to identify whether the poison is contact, ingested or inhaled.
conditions: A yew leaf turns brown when poison is found; several leaves may be needed.
exceptions: A failed poison-type roll prevents further type identification with that casting.
Scanning part of a pond does not establish the condition of the entire pond.

spells.name: Detect Balance

fields.Area: One object or creature per round

effect: Reveals whether a subject’s alignment has no neutral component, a partial neutral component, or is true neutral.
conditions: A partly neutral alignment gives a mild aura; an alignment without neutrality gives a strong aura.
exceptions: Does not distinguish good from evil or lawful from chaotic.
Nonliving objects without a natural alignment aura reveal nothing; unknowable alignment or similar magic conceals an aura.

spells.name: Flame Blade

fields.Materials: Mistletoe and a sumac leaf

effect: Produces a fiery blade wielded like a scimitar; a hit deals 5–8 damage and can ignite combustible material.
conditions: Damage increases by 2 against undead or creatures especially vulnerable to fire; fire protection reduces damage by 2.
exceptions: Cannot harm fire-dwellers or creatures that use fire attacks.
Except against undead, it does not overcome a requirement for magic weapons.
Cannot function underwater except inside airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Goodberry

fields.Materials: Freshly picked edible berries and mistletoe

effect: Enchants 2–8 berries; one can supply a full meal to a hungry creature of roughly human size, or heal 1 hp of wounds.
conditions: Healing is limited to 8 hp per creature in any 24 hours.
The caster, another druid of at least 3rd level, or detect magic can identify enchanted berries.
exceptions: The reverse, badberry, disguises rotten berries as sound; each deals 1 poison damage when eaten, without a save.

spells.name: Reflecting Pool

fields.Area: Natural pool up to 2 feet diameter/level
fields.Materials: Mistletoe; three measures of refined hickory, walnut or similar nut oil

effect: Turns a natural pool into a scrying surface.
Detect magic, detect snares and pits, and detect poison can operate through it with a 5% chance per level; infravision, ultravision, starshine and moonbeam function normally.
conditions: Planar reach is restricted to planes coexistent with or bordering the Prime Material; crystal-ball planar penalties apply.
exceptions: Underwater, any watery space can serve (UA p.81).

spells.name: Alarm

fields.Materials: Tiny bell and fine silver wire

effect: Contact by a living creature larger than a normal rat triggers one segment of loud ringing, ordinarily audible within 60 feet.
conditions: Intervening doors reduce audible radius by 10 feet; substantial walls reduce it by 20 feet.
exceptions: Undead, ethereal creatures and astrally projected creatures do not trigger it.
Living invisible, extraplanar, flying and levitating creatures can trigger it.

spells.name: Armor

fields.Duration: Until dispelled or cumulative damage exceeds 8 + caster level
fields.Materials: Finely cured leather blessed by a cleric

effect: Creates protection equivalent to leather armor (AC 8), without weight, encumbrance or interference with movement or spellcasting.
conditions: A creature whose natural AC is better than 9 improves that AC by one step.
exceptions: Does nothing for a recipient already wearing armor.
Cannot combine with protective magic devices other than a ring of protection.
The damage threshold ends the protection; it does not prevent that damage.

spells.name: Firewater

fields.Materials: Sugar grains and a raisin

effect: Changes water into a lighter, flammable liquid; exposed creatures suffer 2d6 damage when it is ignited.
conditions: Must be ignited within 10 segments; it evaporates after one round even in a sealed container.
exceptions: When cast underwater, it rises to the surface and cannot be ignited underwater (UA p.82).

spells.name: Grease

fields.Materials: Pork rind, butter or similar grease

effect: Coats an area with slippery grease; a creature stepping on it must save versus petrification or fall.
Can instead coat an object such as a rope, ladder rung or weapon handle.
conditions: A held or used object is affected only if its user fails a spell save.
exceptions: An aware creature may avoid the area; a successful save against the object use negates its effect.

spells.name: Run

fields.Materials: Elixir of dried-plum juice in spring water and oil from 5–8 castor beans

effect: Lets recipients run at twice normal speed for 5–8 hours without tiring.
conditions: Afterward they must rest for an equal period, drink plentifully and eat heartily.
Additional recipients are allowed at one per two caster levels, as illustrated at levels 4 and 6.
exceptions: Works only on humans and demi-humans in their natural forms.
Barbarians with their class’s special running ability are immune.

spells.name: Flaming Sphere

fields.Area: 6-foot sphere; creatures within 5 feet of its center
fields.Materials: Tallow, sulphur and powdered iron

effect: Creates a rolling sphere of normal fire that deals 2d4 damage and ignites flammable material.
It moves 1″ per round while the caster points, and can cross barriers up to 4 feet high.
conditions: Without direction it stays in place.
exceptions: A successful saving throw negates the sphere, as stated in the description.
Normal methods for extinguishing a fire of that size work.
Cannot be used underwater except within airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Protection From Cantrips
effect: Protects a touched person or object from cantrips; a cantrip directed at it disperses with a popping noise.
conditions: An unwilling creature must be hit by touch and can save versus spell.
exceptions: This protection concerns cantrips, not ordinary spells.

spells.name: Tasha’s Uncontrollable Hideous Laughter

fields.Materials: Feather, small wooden paddle and a tiny tort

effect: On the round after casting, the target collapses laughing; the next round is spent getting up.
On the third and fourth rounds after casting, strength is reduced by 2, or attacks and damage take a −2 penalty.
conditions: A spell save negates the effect: Intelligence 4–8 saves at −6, 9–12 at −4, 13–15 at −2, and 16+ normally.
exceptions: Creatures with Intelligence 3 or lower are unaffected.

spells.name: Melf’s Acid Arrow

fields.Materials: Dart, powdered rhubarb leaf and adder stomach

effect: Attacks as a same-level fighter using a +1 arrow; an arrow hit deals 2–5 damage, plus 2–8 acid damage in a 1-foot diameter area.
Acid can harm targets that resist the arrow’s weapon damage; items may need saves.
conditions: Neutralizing the acid stops continuing acid damage.
exceptions: No splash damage.
The OCR’s duration formula and example conflict; the exact duration progression is not extracted here.
Underwater, the acid lasts only one round before washing away (UA p.82).

spells.name: Phantom Armor

fields.Materials: Mithral plate worth 10 gp; consumed

effect: Provides quasi-real plate protection (AC 3 and armor type 3), plus +1 to saves against attacks for which magic armor gives a bonus.
Absorbs 1 damage per caster level from blows that would hit AC 3; excess damage reaches the wearer.
conditions: An opponent can actively disbelieve with a spell save.
exceptions: Ends when its damage capacity is spent, dispelled, or negated.
Does not combine with other magical protection and does not hinder movement or spellcasting.

spells.name: Spook
effect: Threateningly advancing on the target makes it perceive a personal fear and flee.
conditions: Each subsequent round gives another spell save, with a cumulative +1 bonus per round.
exceptions: Carried items are not dropped.
Only affects creatures with Intelligence of at least 1.

spells.name: Whispering Wind

fields.Duration: Special; expires after 2 hours at most

effect: Sends a quiet message of up to 12 words, another sound lasting 12 seconds, or a faint rustling to a chosen destination.
Travels at a chosen rate from 1″ to 20″ per round, then lingers for two segments.
conditions: Disappears after delivery, if the objective is out of range, if dispelled, or after two hours.
exceptions: Cannot carry a spell.
Does not function underwater except within airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Phantom Steed
effect: Creates a quiet mount for the caster or a specifically designated rider; maximum movement is 4″ per caster level.
At caster levels 8, 10, 12 and 14 it gains, respectively, easy travel over soft ground, water travel, air-as-ground travel, then pegasus-like flight.
conditions: Carries its rider and carried equipment, with saddle and bridle but no saddlebags.
exceptions: Cannot fight; disappears after taking more than 12 damage.
Underwater it appears as a hippocampus and gains no special travel or flight abilities (UA p.82).

spells.name: Wraithform

fields.Materials: Gauze and a wisp of smoke

effect: Makes the caster and worn or held gear insubstantial, able to pass through tiny cracks.
Normally requires +1 or better magic weapons, or equivalent creature attacks, to hit.
conditions: Most undead ignore the caster; liches and special undead can recognize the magic with a spell save at −4.
exceptions: Cannot attack except against creatures on the Ethereal Plane, where attacks in both directions are normal.
Dispel illusion or dispel magic can end it; voluntarily resuming normal form also ends it.

spells.name: Solid Fog

fields.Materials: Powdered dried peas and animal hoof

effect: Creates dense fog; a creature moves only 1 foot through it for each 1″ of normal movement per round.
conditions: Only a very strong wind moves it.
exceptions: Gust of wind does not affect it.
Fireball, flame strike or wall of fire burns it away in one round.
Cannot function underwater except inside airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Death’s Door

fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol, white linen and unguent

effect: Raises an unconscious human or demi-human at −1 to −9 hp to 0 hp, stopping bleeding and further deterioration for the duration.
conditions: The recipient remains unconscious until healing restores hp.
exceptions: Healing spells, potions and magic items can now restore hp and consciousness.

spells.name: Negative Plane Protection
effect: On an energy-draining undead’s hit, the recipient saves versus death magic: success prevents the experience drain and deals 2d6 damage to the undead, while normal physical damage remains.
conditions: The protection expires after that attack, whether the save succeeds or fails.
exceptions: Failure means the normal experience drain and double physical damage.
Also protects against a magic-user’s energy drain, but does not harm that caster.
Cannot be cast on the Negative Material Plane.

spells.name: Remove Paralysis
effect: Grants new saves versus paralyzation against paralysis or similar effects such as hold: +3 for one target, +2 each for two, or +1 each for three or four.
conditions: Any physical or magical barrier between caster and subjects spoils the spell.
exceptions: The reverse requires a hit with the holy/unholy symbol; a failed spell save paralyzes one creature for 1d6 rounds + 1 round/level.
Some good religious orders prohibit or restrict the reverse.

spells.name: Water Walk

fields.Materials: Cork and holy/unholy symbol

effect: Lets a human-sized recipient walk on water as if on firm grass.
conditions: Each caster level beyond 5 adds capacity for another human-sized creature; a horse counts as six humans.
exceptions: When cast underwater, the recipient immediately bobs to the surface (UA p.81).

spells.name: Cloak of Fear

fields.Materials: Miniature quiver and chicken feather; reverse uses alcohol and newt brain

effect: An intruder failing a spell save flees for six rounds; the aura ends on the first such failure.
conditions: The caster can dismiss the aura; companions are also vulnerable.
exceptions: Undead and fear-radiating creatures are unaffected and do not expend it.
The reverse grants one willing recipient +3 on one save against magical fear; it ends after that save, successful or not.

spells.name: Spell Immunity

fields.Materials: Those required by the selected spell, if any

effect: Protects against one particular spell of 4th level or below which the cleric has directly experienced.
conditions: Does not work on someone already protected by another spell or temporary magical effect.
Only one spell immunity can operate on a recipient at a time.
exceptions: Does not protect possessions, block magic-item effects or innate spell-like powers, or cover a whole family of similar spells.

spells.name: Air Walk

fields.Area: One creature up to giant size
fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol and thistledown

effect: Permits walking on air: ascent at 45°, 60° or straight upward uses half, quarter or eighth normal movement respectively; corresponding descents can use twice, four times or eight times normal movement.
conditions: The traveller controls speed and can stop abruptly.
In gust of wind, movement is halved against the gust or doubled with it.
exceptions: A mount needs training to avoid panic.
Cannot function underwater except within airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Forbiddance

fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol and water; silver/dung and iron/sulfur

effect: Secures a consecrated area. Matching ethics and morals require a password, with no save.
Different ethics require a spell save to enter or cause 2d6 damage; different morals require another save or cause 4d6 damage.
conditions: Effects accumulate when both differences apply.
After a failed save, the intruder cannot enter until the spell ends.
exceptions: The caster is exempt; intruders admitted by successful saves still feel uneasy.

spells.name: Heroes’ Feast

fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol and fermented honey from royal bee-larva cells

effect: Creates a furnished feast. Completing it cures diseases, heals 5–8 hp, and grants bless benefits plus immunity to poison, fear, hopelessness and panic.
conditions: The feast must be consumed for one uninterrupted hour before benefits begin.
exceptions: Any interruption ruins the feast and cancels all its magical benefits.

spells.name: Starshine

fields.Materials: Amaryllis stalks and holly berries

effect: Lights the area like a clear starry night: clear vision to 30 feet, indistinct to 60 feet, then only glimmers.
conditions: Shadows remain; ultravision works at full potential and infravision is unaffected.
exceptions: Disbelieving the apparent night sky only reveals that the stars are magical lights.

spells.name: Moonbeam

fields.Materials: Moonseed seeds and moonstone

effect: Places soft moonlight where the druid points, and can move to another visible, indicated location.
Allows only black, white and gray distinctions; a creature centered in the beam is clearly under observation.
conditions: Shadows remain; infravision is unaffected and ultravision is enhanced.
exceptions: The reflected light permits dim visual perception 1″ beyond the area of effect.

spells.name: Spike Stones

fields.Area: 1 square ″/level; one spike per square foot
fields.Materials: Four tiny stalactites

effect: Turns natural or worked stone into concealed spikes. Each successful attack-like check uses the caster’s attack ability and deals 1d4 damage.
conditions: Careful observers have a 25% chance to notice the spikes.
Attacks occur on entry and subsequent steps; charging/running victims face two further attacks per 1″ of movement before halting, others one.
exceptions: Falling into a spiked pit causes six checks per 10 feet fallen, with +2 to hit and damage per 10 feet, in addition to falling damage.

spells.name: Liveoak

fields.Materials: Mistletoe

effect: Enchants an oak to become a treant-like guardian when a programmed condition occurs; its movement is 3″.
conditions: The oak must be within 10 feet of the druid’s home, in a sacred place, or within 10″ of something to guard.
The trigger may contain up to one word/caster level; only one liveoak from the druid can operate at once.
exceptions: Dispel magic or the druid’s choice returns it to normal.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Changestaff

fields.Duration: 1 turn/level per transformation, or until ended
fields.Materials: Prepared ash, oak or yew staff; mistletoe or matching leaves

effect: Changes a prepared staff into an obedient treant-like defender, initially 12 HD and 96 hp; planting it and speaking the prayer activates it.
It can return to staff form on command and be transformed again.
conditions: Preparation needs a sound limb from a tree struck by lightning within 24 hours, 28 days curing and 28 days crafting without adventure or strenuous activity, then holly juice and a speak with plants rite.
Each 8 damage permanently removes one HD and shrinks its combat power.
exceptions: Below 7 HD it crumbles; only wish restores lost HD/hp.
It cannot converse with true treants.

spells.name: Transmute Water To Dust

fields.Materials: Diamond dust worth at least 500 gp, seashell and mistletoe

effect: Turns existing water into dust: muddy water doubles affected volume and wet mud quadruples it.
Water-containing potions are ruined; later water can soak the dust back into mud.
conditions: Only one native of the Elemental Plane of Water can be affected, with a spell save.
exceptions: Other living creatures are unaffected.
The reverse creates water and also requires ordinary dust.
Underwater it opens a 10-cubic-foot/level hole; rushing water deals 1d4/level damage to those inside without saves (UA p.81).

spells.name: Melf’s Minute Meteors

fields.Duration: Until missiles are used, abandoned or dispelled
fields.Materials: Nitre and sulphur in pine tar; reusable gold tube worth at least 1,000 gp

effect: Provides one thrown fire missile per caster level; each deals 1d4 damage and can ignite combustibles. Misses use grenade-like missile handling.
conditions: Choose once: fire every two segments, or one each round.
The once-per-round option permits another spell that does not need continuing concentration.
exceptions: Switching firing options is prohibited; abandoning fire, losing exact missile count or taking up continuing concentration forfeits the remainder.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Evard’s Black Tentacles

fields.Saving throw: Special: spell save on contact in description
fields.Materials: Giant octopus or squid tentacle

effect: Creates one 10-foot tentacle/caster level, each AC 4 with hp equal to caster level.
A victim saving versus spell takes 1d4 damage and destroys that tentacle; failure takes 2d4 damage, then 3d4 each later round while wrapped.
conditions: Targets within reach are selected without intelligence; when several are available, determine the target randomly.
exceptions: Tentacles can grip objects or keep squeezing a corpse; a grip persists until the tentacle is destroyed or the spell expires.
The header says no save, while the paragraph expressly grants one.

spells.name: Leomund’s Secure Shelter

fields.Materials: Stone chip, lime, sand, water and wood; alarm/servant also require bell, silver wire and string

effect: Creates a furnished cottage from local materials, with the strength and fire resistance of stone and resistance to winds up to 70 mph.
Doors and shutters are wizard locked; the chimney has a grate and narrow flue. With the required extra components, alarm wards and an unseen servant are included.
conditions: Provides no artificial heating or cooling.
exceptions: Normal missiles are stopped, but giant-thrown and siege missiles can penetrate.

spells.name: Otiluke’s Resilient Sphere

fields.Materials: Matching hemispheres of hard clear gemstone and gum arabic

effect: Encloses a creature that fits and fails its spell save. Nothing passes through, but the creature can breathe.
conditions: Struggles inside or forces outside can physically move the sphere.
exceptions: A cancellation rod, negation wand, disintegrate or dispel magic destroys it without harming the occupant; other damage does not.

spells.name: Stoneskin

fields.Materials: Granite and diamond dust sprinkled on skin

effect: Stops one opponent’s attack or attack sequence involving cuts, blows or projectiles, even from powerful weapons.
conditions: That attack sequence normally expends the protection.
exceptions: Spell attacks such as fireball, magic missile and lightning bolt work normally.
Relatively soft attacks such as fists deal 1–2 hp to their attacker instead and do not expend the protection.

spells.name: Fabricate

fields.Casting time: 1 round/cubic yard, or cubic foot for minerals

effect: Converts raw material into a product of essentially that material, such as timber into a bridge or wool into clothing.
conditions: Product quality depends on the material; work requiring great craftsmanship also requires the caster to possess that craft skill.
exceptions: Cannot create or alter magical or living things.

spells.name: Chain Lightning

fields.Saving throw: Half damage; secondary targets also save to avoid a hit
fields.Area: Up to one successful link/caster level
fields.Materials: Fur; amber, glass or crystal rod; one silver pin/caster level

effect: The first hit deals 1d6/caster level, and each subsequent hit deals one fewer d6.
Arcs seek the nearest object, including creatures, plants and minerals; a secondary target’s successful spell save diverts the arc, while a separate damage save halves damage.
conditions: Equidistant choices prefer metal, then the greater fluid content, otherwise random; targets can be struck repeatedly.
An arc beyond the spell’s range ends the chain; a tree or substantial conductive metal can ground it.
exceptions: The caster can be hit.
Underwater it acts like a double-radius lightning bolt for 1d6/level, save for half (UA p.82).

spells.name: Contingency

fields.Materials: Companion’s components, quicksilver worth 100 gp, ivory self-statuette and eyelash of a spell-using creature

effect: Prepares a personal spell to trigger instantly when a stated event occurs.
conditions: The companion must affect the caster and be no higher than one-third caster level, rounded down, with a maximum spell level of 6.
The ivory statuette survives casting and must be carried for the trigger to work.
exceptions: Only one contingency can operate; casting another cancels the first.
Overly complicated trigger conditions can make both spells fail.

spells.name: Alter Self
effect: Makes a partly real change of form, permitting size changes of up to 50%.
Gills permit underwater breathing; wings permit flight at one-quarter the true creature’s speed and two maneuverability classes worse, no worse than E.
conditions: Extra attacks or damage from a larger form require familiarity with that form.

spells.name: Rainbow Pattern

fields.Materials: Crystal prism and phosphor

effect: Creates a hypnotic display that can draw affected creatures totaling up to 24 levels or HD along with it.
Gesturing moves the pattern at 3″ per round.
conditions: Affected creatures receive another save if led into danger.
exceptions: Completely blocking their view of the lights ends the effect.

spells.name: Advanced Illusion

fields.Materials: Fleece and sand grains

effect: Creates a spectral-forces-like illusion that operates through a program similar to programmed illusion, with visual, full sound, smell and heat sensations.
conditions: Only five segments of concentration after casting are needed to start the program.
exceptions: Active disbelief permits a spell save; a successful disbeliever who communicates the discovery gives comprehending viewers saves at +4.

spells.name: Death Fog

fields.Materials: Powdered dry peas, animal hoof and strong acid

effect: Creates acidic solid fog. Animal life not immune to acid takes 1, 2, 4, then 8 hp in the first, second, third, and fourth/subsequent exposure rounds.
conditions: Plants die after exposure: small plants 2 rounds, shrubs 4, small trees 8, large trees 16.
Otherwise retains solid fog’s severe movement restriction and resistance to ordinary wind.
exceptions: As solid fog, gust of wind fails; fireball, flame strike or wall of fire burns it away in one round.
Cannot function underwater except within airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Mislead
effect: Combines improved invisibility for the caster with a phantasmal double that can move, speak and gesture, with smell and touch sensations.
conditions: The caster can move away while the double appears to depart.
exceptions: Detect illusion, true sight/seeing or a gem of seeing reveals the double.
Detect invisibility, true sight/seeing, a gem of seeing or a robe of eyes can reveal the hidden caster.

spells.name: Shadow Walk
effect: From heavy shadow, moves the party to the border of the Prime Material and Shadow planes, allowing travel at up to seven leagues per turn.
conditions: The caster controls the intended Prime Material destination; reaching other planes requires hazardous travel through Shadow.
exceptions: Touched companions can choose not to follow; abandoned or lost companions have a 50% chance of wandering into Shadow, otherwise returning to the Prime Material.
The header lists no save, but the paragraph allows unwilling travellers a saving throw.

spells.name: Ceremony

fields.Materials: Holy symbol; additional requirements vary by religion

effect: Provides distinct religious rites, not one general blessing: coming of age, burial and marriage are available at cleric level 1; dedication, investiture and item consecration at 3; ordination and special vows at 5; ground consecration at 7; anathematizing at 9.
Coming of age grants one future +1 save; burial protects a corpse for a week; investiture and ordination establish religious standing.
Special vows protect a cavalier/paladin from bestow curse, but impose −4 against a same-alignment cleric’s quest.
conditions: The listed cleric rank is a minimum. All rites except anathematizing require willingness.
Ground must be consecrated before construction begins; consecrated graveyards turn or protect undead as a 3rd-level cleric.
exceptions: Anathematizing allows an unwilling subject a spell save at −4 and fails if undeserved; atonement can reduce or remove the brand.
This card condenses nine rites; detailed religious requirements and service costs remain in the source.

spells.name: Combine
effect: Three to five clerics cast together; the highest-level cleric stands in the middle and gains one effective level per encircling cleric, to a maximum gain of four.
The boost affects turning and level-dependent spell results, without granting additional prepared spells.
conditions: Encircling clerics must hold hands and concentrate.
exceptions: They lose shield and Dexterity AC benefits, and attacks against them gain +4.

spells.name: Endure Cold / Endure Heat
effect: Protects against normal cold down to −30°F or normal heat up to 130°F, depending on the chosen application; beyond the limit, exposure causes 1 hp/hour per excess degree instead of 1 hp/turn.
conditions: The selected cold or heat application does not restrict which magical temperature effect cancels it.
exceptions: Any magical heat or cold ends it, but the recipient avoids damage from that event during the round of cancellation.
Resist fire or resist cold immediately cancels it.

spells.name: Invisibility to Undead

fields.Materials: Holy symbol

effect: For each type of undead of 4 HD or fewer within 30 feet, roll one spell save: failure makes that type ignore the caster, while success makes it prefer attacking the caster.
conditions: Morally neutral casters impose −2 on the undead’s saves.
exceptions: Attacking or attempting another spell ends the effect; ignored undead cannot subsequently be turned by the caster during it.
The text describes its effect on the caster despite the header allowing one touched individual; application to another recipient needs adjudication.

spells.name: Magic Stone

fields.Area: One ordinary stone, increasing with caster level

effect: Enchants an ordinary pebble for throwing: +1 to hit, but only 1 hp damage. Another person may throw it.
Caster levels 6–10 enchant two stones, 11–15 three, then one more each five levels.
conditions: A miss, travel beyond 4″, or six rounds without use ends the enchantment.
exceptions: Does not affect already-magical stones or targets with innate magic resistance.
Shield, brooch of shielding, protection from normal missiles, minor globe of invulnerability and stronger similar magic stop it.
A struck spellcaster loses concentration only on a failed spell save; some religions prohibit its use.

spells.name: Penetrate Disguise
effect: Identifies that someone is using a nonmagical makeup/clothing disguise; it can also reveal a friends spell.
conditions: Bless, magic armor and protective magic can improve the subject’s save.
exceptions: A successful subject save instead convinces the caster that the assumed identity is authentic.
Does not disclose true appearance, class, rank, alignment deception or illusions.

spells.name: Portent

fields.Materials: Numbered wheel or tea leaves

effect: The DM secretly rolls d12 to select a later life-or-death attack/save roll and d6 to assign a good or bad modifier from −3 to +3, excluding zero.
The caster learns whether the omen is good, fair or poor; the exact affected roll remains unknown.
conditions: Count the recipient’s attacks and saves and opponents’ attacks against that recipient.
exceptions: Harmless, contrived tests do not advance the count or bypass the omen.

spells.name: Precipitation

fields.Materials: Pinch of silver dust

effect: Creates light rain: exposed small flames go out after one segment; small fires become smoky, while large fires are largely unaffected.
Thin/nonporous surfaces dampen in one segment; twigs/canvas and semiporous surfaces take two to dampen, with semiporous material thoroughly wet after five.
conditions: Above 90°F, duration doubles except in arid regions; near freezing it becomes sleet, at 30°F or lower snow.
exceptions: Large-area magical heat turns it into warm fog covering double the area; magical cold freezes the remaining water.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Dust Devil
effect: Summons a weak air elemental: AC 4, 2 HD, movement 18″ and one attack for 1d4 damage. Magic weapons deal it double damage.
Can push back gas and extinguish small nonmagical flames; over loose dust/sand/ash it creates a 30-foot cloud that blinds victims until one round after leaving.
conditions: It follows direction but vanishes if ordered beyond 3″; a caster inside it must save versus spell to preserve concentration even without taking damage.
exceptions: Any creature native to the Elemental Plane of Air, including another dust devil, can dismiss it within 3″; creatures not native to the plane occupied by the caster are unaffected.
Innate magic resistance dispels it after it gets a chance to hit.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Enthrall
effect: Captivates listeners who understand the language, making them regard the caster as Charisma 21 and listen attentively.
conditions: Only subjects of 4 levels/HD or fewer and Wisdom 15 or below are eligible; generally unfriendly races save at +4.
Offensive religious/alignment preaching grants offended listeners another save at +5.
exceptions: It does not make listeners obey as suggestion would.
Stopping speech, another action/spell, or an attack against the cleric ends it.
Successful savers see Charisma 3 and may jeer, permitting others another save.

spells.name: Messenger

fields.Materials: Food appealing to the animal

effect: Calls a small animal to carry an attached note or item to a simply described location, and optionally wait there until the duration ends.
conditions: The animal must have at least animal intelligence and be below Intelligence 4, or below low intelligence, whichever classification applies; giant forms are excluded.
exceptions: The receiver gains no ability to communicate with it and may overlook it; the animal resumes normal activity afterward.

spells.name: Withdraw

fields.Duration: Special; duration formula/example disagree in OCR

effect: Gives the cleric one round of contemplation per segment passing outside, with real-world thinking time allowed by the DM.
Permits thinking, reading, and casting augury, informational or healing magic only upon the caster.
conditions: No discussion with unaffected companions is allowed.
exceptions: Moving, becoming invisible, acting outside the permitted scope, casting on someone else or suffering a successful attack ends it.
The stated time-budget formula and 5th-level example conflict; no general duration calculation is supplied here.

spells.name: Cloudburst

fields.Materials: Powdered silver, iodine crystals and holy symbol

effect: Produces a downpour that drenches the area within one segment and extinguishes normal fires: small immediately, medium in 3–5 segments and large in 8–10.
Large magical fires form steam covering four times the area, dealing 1d3 damage/round, doubled against cold-dwellers/users.
conditions: Steam persists 2–5 rounds, halved in a breeze or one round in strong wind; permanent magical fires relight in 1–2 rounds.
exceptions: In arid regions it is only double precipitation; hot humid regions extend it to two rounds. Near freezing it becomes sleet or snow.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Flame Walk

fields.Materials: At least 500 gp powdered ruby and holy/unholy symbol

effect: Protects against nonmagical fire up to 2,000°F and grants +2 on saves against magical fire.
conditions: Capacity starts at one human-sized recipient; each caster level above 5 adds another. A horse counts as six humans, halfling-sized creatures as half, and pixie-sized creatures as a quarter.
exceptions: Magical fire protection is a saving-throw bonus, not complete immunity.

spells.name: Magical Vestment

fields.Materials: Vestment and holy/unholy symbol

effect: Makes vestments protect as chain mail while on ground consecrated to the caster’s deity.
If no armor or protective device is worn, adds +1 enchantment per four cleric levels, to +4 maximum (base AC 1).
conditions: The caster must remain conscious and inside the consecrated ground.
exceptions: Wearing other armor/protection limits it to ordinary chain-mail protection.

spells.name: Meld Into Stone

fields.Area: Caster and up to 100 lb nonliving gear
fields.Materials: Sample of the stone entered

effect: Hides the caster inside a stone large enough for the body in all dimensions; the caster senses time but cannot see or hear outside.
The caster may leave early through the same face used to enter.
conditions: Artifacts/relics are excluded; excess gear or inadequate stone makes casting fail.
exceptions: Expiry ejects the caster for 4d8 damage; gear must save versus petrification or become stone.
Stone to flesh ejects for 4d8; stone shape deals 4d4 without ejecting; transmute rock to mud ejects and kills unless a spell save succeeds.
It cannot be used to pass through the stone.

spells.name: Abjure

fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol and water; substance inimical to target

effect: Attempts to return an extraplanar creature home using the dispel-magic-style caster-level/creature-HD comparison, with a base 50% chance.
conditions: The creature’s exact type and any proper name must be known.
exceptions: Does not affect deities, though their servants may be eligible.
The reverse, implore, calls a like-aligned creature using desirable/respected material instead; arrival grants no assurance of cooperation.
The header and paragraph use different save/procedure wording; consult the source before resolving the detailed check.

spells.name: Giant Insect

fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol

effect: Enlarges ordinary insects. At caster levels 7–9, 10–11, 12–13 and 14+, maximum insect counts are 1/2/3/4 and total HD limits are 3/4/5/6 respectively.
Uses the giant form’s physical characteristics, but damage is reduced if HD are lower and never exceeds its normal damage.
conditions: Only simple orders work; otherwise they attack nearby targets. They do not attack the cleric.
An interruption during casting kills the subjects.
exceptions: Arachnids/crustaceans are excluded; created forms gain no giant-form special attacks or defenses.
The reverse shrinks giant insects by 1 HD per 4 caster levels, up to 6 HD reduction, to a minimum of ⅛ HD or 1 hp.

spells.name: Imbue With Spell Ability

fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol and a consumed token of recipient’s profession

effect: Transfers prepared informational/defensive spells or cure light wounds: at most two 1st-level and one 2nd-level spell.
Recipient needs Wisdom 9+, at least one full HD, level 3+ for two 1st-level spells, and level 5+ for a 2nd-level spell.
conditions: Eligible classes: fighter, thief, cavalier, assassin, monk, ranger below 8, paladin below 9; no monsters or other classes.
Level-dependent effects use the recipient’s level.
exceptions: Including an ineligible spell ruins the whole transfer.
The paragraph states that the cleric cannot memorize more spells until all transferred spells are used.

spells.name: Spike Growth

fields.Materials: Holy symbol and seven sharp thorns or sharpened twigs

effect: Hardens plants or roots into concealed spikes. Each 1″ of travel causes two attack checks using the caster’s attack ability, each hit dealing 1d4.
conditions: Requires vegetation or underlying roots; magical detection such as true seeing or detect traps reveals it.
exceptions: Vegetation-controlling/harming magic or dispel magic negates it.
The description calls this level 4; the spell list labels it level 5. This card follows the description and preserves the disagreement.

spells.name: Animate Dead Monsters

fields.Area: One corpse/skeleton per two caster levels
fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol and a specimen of the creature type
fields.Monster zombie baseline: MM2 p.131: AC 6, move 9″, 6 HD, 1 attack for 4–16 damage; strikes last, takes half damage from blunt weapons, immune to charm, cold, death magic, hold and sleep, turned as a ghast, and takes 2–8 damage per vial of holy water. UA p.39 specifies normal physical attacks for these animated monsters and uses normal living statistics instead when the original creature has fewer than 6 HD.

effect: Animates large humanoid or semihumanoid remains and permits commands of about 12 words.
Skeletons have half normal HD rounded up; corpses generally use monster-zombie rules, or normal creature statistics if the original has fewer than 6 HD.
conditions: Normally needs bipedal endoskeletal creatures over 7 feet tall with more than 3 HD.
exceptions: Retains physical attacks, but not original special attacks/defenses beyond those of the undead form.

spells.name: Golem

fields.Lesser golem statistics: Straw: AC 10, MV 12″, HD 2+4, hp 20, 2 attacks for 1–2/1–2 damage; immune to piercing, half damage from blunt weapons, double damage from flame; carries 30 lb. Rope: AC 8, MV 9″, HD 3+6, hp 30, 1 attack for 1–6 damage plus strangulation (6 points per round after a hit until destroyed or made to release its grip); immune to blunt, half damage from piercing; carries 40 lb. Leather: AC 6, MV 6″, HD 4+8, hp 40, 2 attacks for 1–6/1–6 damage; hit only by +1 or better magic weapon, half damage from blunt; carries 50 lb. Wood: AC 4, MV 3″, HD 5+10, hp 50, 1 attack for 3–12 damage; hit only by +1 or better magic weapon, immune to blunt and piercing; carries 60 lb.

effect: Animates a personally constructed, humanoid-shaped body 3–7 feet tall after prayer is cast on it.
Straw/rope/leather/wood forms require caster levels 9/11/13/15; construction takes 1/3/9/27 hours and animation lasts 1/3/6/12 hours per caster level respectively.
conditions: Understands simple orders of up to about 12 words; saves as a cleric of the creator’s level.
exceptions: Mind-affecting spells such as charm, fear, hold and sleep do not affect it.

spells.name: Magic Font

fields.Duration: 1 round per vial of basin capacity
fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol, font and trappings; not consumed

effect: Turns a holy/unholy water font into a crystal-ball-like scrying device.
conditions: The cleric must be in good standing with the deity; use crystal-ball and magic-mirror rules for observation and detection.
exceptions: Underwater, use a glass globe of pure water instead of a font (UA p.81).

spells.name: Rainbow

fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol and water; a prepared diamond may substitute for a visible rainbow

effect: Bow: a +3 bow with seven arrows, usable at one or two shots/round by a bow-using class with Strength 6+. Each hue has specific doubled-damage foes, not fully listed here.
Bridge: 20–120 feet long, caster-level feet wide, carrying 100 lb/level; exceeding capacity removes it.
Elevator: lifts the caster and those within 10 feet at 12″ movement.
Flagon: seven drinks provide cure light wounds, resist fire, cure blindness, slow poison, cure disease, resist cold and remove paralysis as a 12th-level cleric.
conditions: Requires a visible rainbow or a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp previously blessed and prayed over in sight of a rainbow.
exceptions: Only the holy symbol survives casting; unused rainbow objects/drinks vanish on expiry, though consumed spell benefits persist normally.

spells.name: Spike Stones

fields.Area: 1 square ″/level; spikes one per square foot
fields.Materials: Four tiny stalactites

effect: Raises concealed sharp points in natural or worked stone. Attacks use the caster’s attack ability and deal 1d4 per successful hit.
Careful examination has a 25% chance to detect them; entry and subsequent steps provoke attacks.
conditions: After initial damage, charging/running victims face two further checks per 1″ of movement before stopping; others face one.
Falling into a spiked pit causes six checks per 10 feet fallen, each +2 to hit/damage per 10 feet, plus normal falling damage.
exceptions: The description calls this level 5; the spell list labels it level 4. This card follows the description.

spells.name: Exaction

fields.Materials: Holy/unholy symbol, matter from its plane and burned written knowledge of the subject

effect: Binds an extraplanar creature to a reasonable service in return for a past favor or promised fair reward, acting like quest.
When service is complete, it returns to the cleric for immediate repayment, then is freed to return home.
conditions: The target cannot be ethically or morally opposed; true neutrality counts as opposed to both ends of each alignment axis.
exceptions: Deities and demigods are excluded.
Reneging can subject the cleric to exaction in return, or make the creature immune to the cleric’s spells while attacking.

spells.name: Succor

fields.Materials: Special prepared object costing 2,000–5,000 gp

effect: Enchants an object that the cleric willingly gives away with a command word; breaking it while saying that word transports its holder and carried gear to the cleric’s sanctuary, as word of recall.
conditions: The reverse summons the cleric to the holder instead.
exceptions: Other creatures cannot accompany the holder.
For the reverse, the cleric may refuse at the instant of summoning, but that wastes the one opportunity.

spells.name: Ceremony

fields.Materials: Mistletoe; a grove or healthy natural forest setting

effect: Provides druidic rites: coming of age/rest eternal/marriage (listed rank 1), dedication/investiture (3), initiation/special vows (7), hallowed ground (9), and cast out (12).
Rest eternal prevents raise dead and resurrection, though wish can restore life; initiation unlocks 7th-level shapechanging and woodland-charm immunity.
Hallowed ground protects a permanent grove from disease and natural disaster; cast out makes natural creatures react negatively.
conditions: Dedication requires true neutrality; special vows apply to cavaliers of any alignment, not paladins.
Cast out needs hierarchical permission; unwilling targets save versus spell at −4.
exceptions: The OCR says the listed ranks are 'indicated or lower'; this contradicts the hierarchy implied by the rites, so minimum-rank wording is not resolved here.
Only a Hierophant Druid can fully cancel casting out; other reversals merely lessen it.

spells.name: Precipitation

fields.Materials: Silver dust and mistletoe

effect: Uses the cleric’s light-rain effects: wets exposed surfaces and extinguishes small flames; large fires are largely unaffected.
conditions: Thin/nonporous material dampens in one segment; twigs/canvas and semiporous material in two, with semiporous material wet through after five.
Above 90°F duration doubles except in arid regions; near freezing it becomes sleet, at 30°F or lower snow.
exceptions: Large magical heat makes warm fog covering double the area; magical cold freezes remaining water.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Slow Poison

fields.Materials: Mistletoe and crushed garlic rubbed on feet
fields.Base rule: PHB pp.45–46; UA p.43 modifies the druid version

effect: Slows rather than neutralizes venom; the PHB rule permits temporary recovery after poisoning within caster-level turns, with 1 hp lost/turn but never below 1 hp while protected.
If the poison is recognized as plant-derived, the druid has a 5% chance/level to know an herbal antidote.
conditions: A successful detect poison type result can identify organic poison; the antidote must then be obtained from green vegetation, an herbalist or similar source.
exceptions: The spell’s ordinary protection ends when its duration expires; knowing an antidote is not the same as already possessing it.

spells.name: Cloudburst

fields.Materials: Powdered silver, iodine crystals, holy symbol as cleric base, plus mistletoe

effect: Uses the cleric’s heavy downpour: instantly drenches the area; extinguishes small fires immediately, medium in 3–5 segments and large in 8–10.
Extinguishing large magical fire creates steam over four times the area, dealing 1d3 damage/round, doubled against cold-dwellers/users.
conditions: Arid conditions reduce it to double precipitation; hot humidity gives two rounds; freezing conditions change it to sleet/snow.
exceptions: It cannot be combined with call lightning or used to call lightning.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Know Alignment

fields.Base rule: PHB p.45; UA p.43 modifies the druid version

effect: Reads a subject’s exact alignment using the cleric spell’s basic effect.
conditions: Can examine at most five creatures because of its shorter duration.
exceptions: Cannot be reversed; some magical devices defeat alignment detection.

spells.name: Spike Growth

fields.Materials: Mistletoe and seven small thorns or sharpened twigs

effect: Hardens vegetation or roots into concealed spikes. Each 1″ moved through it causes two attacks using the caster’s attack ability, each successful hit dealing 1d4.
conditions: Unlike the cleric version, the druid’s area radiates magic, and detect snares and pits reveals it.
exceptions: Vegetation-controlling/harming magic and dispel magic negate it.

spells.name: Sunray

fields.Area: 1″ diameter sphere, plus a 2″ peripheral zone
fields.Materials: Aster seed and sunstone

effect: Creates sunlight-like radiance: ordinary creatures failing a spell save are blinded for 1d3 rounds; ultravision users may be blinded 2d4 rounds; sunlight-harmed creatures risk permanent blindness.
Undead in the main area take 8d6 damage, save for half; those in the peripheral zone take 3d6, save for none.
conditions: Creatures normally harmed by sunlight that save are still blinded 2d6 rounds; infravision in the main/peripheral areas is lost for 2–5 rounds.
exceptions: Fungoid creatures and subterranean fungi take undead-like damage without a save.

spells.name: Colored Lights

fields.Area: One 1-foot globe, two 6-inch, three 4-inch or four 3-inch globes

effect: Creates movable pastel lights, each illuminating a radius five times its diameter.
conditions: Globes stay near the caster, floating or resting as directed.
exceptions: Reflections extend no farther than 1″ and their light cannot be detected beyond 3″.
Pale blue/pink leaves infravision and ultravision unaffected; other hues interfere with those senses.

spells.name: Dim
effect: Weakens torches, candles, a medium fire, or light/continual light, reducing radiance to at most half normal.
conditions: Affected lights must be within range.
exceptions: Affects about 6 torches, a medium fire, 72 candles, or a light or continual light spell.

spells.name: Haze
effect: Creates a dusty/smoky screen: missile attacks through it take −1, spell saves gain +1, and hiding in shadows improves by 5%.
conditions: A spell normally allowing no save instead permits a 5% chance to save against a screened target.
exceptions: Breeze, rain and similar conditions destroy it; gust of wind disperses it immediately.

spells.name: Mask
effect: Illusorily changes the subject’s face, hair, ears and head shape.
conditions: The caster chooses the desired features while touching the caster’s own face.
exceptions: Close scrutiny or active detect illusion can expose the mask.

spells.name: Mirage
effect: Covers a relatively flat, featureless area with the appearance of a real place the caster has personally seen.
conditions: Each round carries a cumulative 5% chance that the scene wavers and reveals itself.
exceptions: Touch, dispel illusion or dispel magic immediately ends it.

spells.name: Noise
effect: Creates indistinct illusory noise such as distant voices, rushing wings, or shuffling and scraping.
conditions: Each listener saves separately; success means that listener does not hear the illusion.
exceptions: It produces confusing impressions rather than a clear spoken message.

spells.name: Rainbow
effect: Creates a glowing pastel ribbon that may bend or move; failed savers watch for 1–4 segments, or 2–5 while it moves.
conditions: Movement requires hand gestures and the caster remaining within 1″.
A stationary rainbow can be left behind.
exceptions: It remains visible in normal darkness.

spells.name: Two-D’lusion
effect: Creates a flat illusion similar in most respects to phantasmal force.
conditions: Viewing more than 45° off its intended axis immediately exposes it.
exceptions: It is invisible from the sides and rear; touch, dispel illusion or dispel magic ends it.

spells.name: Chromatic Orb

fields.Range: Created in hand; thrown up to 3″
fields.Materials: Appropriately colored or clear gem worth at least 50 gp
fields.Damage/effect table: 1st pearly: 1–4/light; 2nd ruby: 1–6/heat; 3rd flame: 1–8/fire; 4th amber: 1–10/blindness; 5th emerald: 1–12/stinking cloud; 6th turquoise: 2–16/magnetism; 7th sapphire: 2–8/paralysis; 10th amethyst: slow/petrification; 12th ashen: paralysis/death.

effect: Creates a colored orb to throw at a creature. Attack bonuses are +3 within 1″, +2 beyond 1″ through 2″, and +1 beyond 2″ through 3″.
Higher caster levels unlock different colors, damage and secondary powers; previously available colors can still be chosen.
conditions: Requires an unobstructed path; magic resistance applies.
exceptions: Can affect creatures otherwise requiring powerful magical weapons; a miss simply dissipates.
Power details, conditions and saving throws are described in the table notes.

spells.name: Read Illusionist Magic
effect: Uses read magic’s basic process specifically for illusionist spells and other inscriptions in illusionist magical script.
exceptions: It does not grant general access to other classes’ magical writing.
The heading marks it reversible, but the reverse’s detailed operation is not separately explained here.

spells.name: Fascinate
effect: Makes the caster appear a trusted or desired companion; the subject follows unless doing so creates undue risk.
For a spoken request, roll 3d6: obedience requires the result not exceed caster comeliness; add +1 against the subject’s interests or +2 to +6 for greater hazards.
conditions: Exceeding comeliness breaks the spell and provokes anger.
Ordinary animals remain affected 1d4 days; good care gives a 2%-per-comeliness chance they stay voluntarily afterward.
exceptions: Non-intelligent creatures are unaffected; neglected animals attack when freed, otherwise leave.

spells.name: Ultravision

fields.Materials: Powdered carrot essence

effect: Provides clear night vision to 100 yards and indistinct vision to roughly 300; very dark cloud cover halves its reach.
As noted for illusionists, high intelligence may allow invisible creatures to be detected with this vision.
conditions: More than 6 feet of earth or 3 feet of stone blocks sky radiation, leaving only dim vision within about 3 feet unless another emission source exists.
exceptions: Nearby bright light, including magical item light, spoils distant ultraviolet perception.

spells.name: Delude
effect: Copies another creature’s apparent alignment aura for alignment-detection magic, without changing that creature’s own alignment.
With change self or alter self, also conceals the caster’s actual class.
conditions: The copied creature must have more than animal intelligence.
exceptions: The copied creature radiates magic; the illusionist radiates magic only to that creature.
The save applies to the aura transfer, not a separate class-disguise check.

spells.name: Phantom Wind
effect: Creates unseen, unfelt wind that moves light objects and gases, flutters cloth, fans fire and can propel sails.
conditions: The path grows in the pointed direction at 1″ per round; wind effects continue along the entire length already reached.
exceptions: Cannot function underwater except inside airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Dispel Magic
effect: Uses the cleric dispel magic rules, treating the illusionist as two experience levels below actual level.
exceptions: For example, a 9th-level illusionist resolves the spell as a 7th-level caster; consult the cleric spell for the underlying dispelling procedure.

spells.name: Vacancy

fields.Materials: Fine black silk worth at least 100 gp

effect: Makes a place appear abandoned and empty, concealing nonliving contents under apparent dust, webs and neglect.
conditions: Brushing an object does not expose it; forceful contact and discovery of several unseen objects permit a spell save. A failed save suggests merely invisible objects.
exceptions: Living creatures remain visible without otherwise disrupting it.
Detect invisibility does not pierce it; true seeing, a gem of seeing or similar effects do. Dispel illusion/magic removes it.

spells.name: Dream
effect: After at least eight hours of undisturbed sleep, brings a strictly limited desired result 1–12 hours later: healing, restored limb, a route/object location or comparable guidance.
A recently dead person dreamed alive lasts only 1 turn/caster level before reverting.
conditions: Use is limited to once per week; a second casting that week fails and ages the caster 1d10 years.
A scried creature with 7+ HD may save, remain undetected and possibly sense the caster.
exceptions: Extension and permanency do not work on it; it cannot grant unrestricted wish effects.

spells.name: Magic Mirror

fields.Materials: Silver mirror worth at least 1,000 gp; bird eye, nitric acid, copper and zinc

effect: Uses the magic-user magic mirror as a crystal-ball-like scrying surface.
Comprehend languages, read magic, tongues, infravision and ultravision work through it; detect magic, detect good/evil, message and detect illusion have a 5% chance/caster level.
conditions: The silver mirror survives; other normal components are consumed.
exceptions: An illusionist may cast vision instead of the normal material components; the mirror works but vision does not give its normal result.
Targets may detect the scrying; consult crystal-ball and magic-mirror detection rules.

spells.name: Tempus Fugit
effect: Speeds those inside to six times perceived time: ten minutes outside seems an hour inside, allowing accelerated rest, spell renewal and healing.
The reverse slows experience so an outside hour seems ten minutes.
conditions: The caster and later entrants are affected; food, sleep and spell durations follow the altered rate.
exceptions: In the reversed version, slow reactions cause at least one turn’s delay after the caster wishes to end it.

spells.name: Phantasmagoria
effect: Prepares a triggered, multisensory spectral-forces-like scene, such as seeming to fall into a deep pit or face a rushing wall of water.
conditions: The trigger can be a fall, entering a location, opening a door or similar action.
exceptions: Unlike an unrestricted programmed illusion, it must involve falling, rushing movement or dwindling perspective.

spells.name: Mirage Arcane

fields.Materials: Optional small object connected to the depicted place

effect: Makes an area resemble an actual place personally seen by the caster; using a related material component gives the illusion greater reality.
conditions: Faint concentration survives conversation, but not spellcasting, melee or being hurt.
exceptions: The basic form needs forceful tactile discovery or magical detection to expose; the material-enhanced form needs magic.
Belief can affect bodily experience, but gravity remains real: an illusory bridge cannot support a traveller.
Dispel illusion or dispel magic removes it.

spells.name: Weird
effect: Confronts subjects with their most feared opponents. Failed savers must fight apparently real duels with no magical escape; defeat causes death.
Defeating the nemesis leaves no damage, item use or spell expenditure, and may earn appropriate XP.
conditions: The caster must communicate the threat and maintain full concentration.
Each apparent combat round takes only one segment of real time.
exceptions: Even on a successful save, fear paralyzes the subject for 7 segments and causes a loss of 1–4 Strength points; the lost Strength returns in 7 rounds.

spells.name: Chill

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes nonliving liquid or solid material about 40°F colder, but not below freezing.
conditions: Cooling is instantaneous; the object then warms normally.

spells.name: Clean

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Removes heavy dirt and foreign matter from surfaces, leaving them spotless.
conditions: Usually treats one material type per casting.
exceptions: Care is needed with pigments and similar material that cleaning might remove.

spells.name: Color

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Changes, restores or brightens an object’s color; can also recolor hair or skin.

spells.name: Dampen

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Leaves material damp and surrounds the area with light fog that obscures fine detail.
Makes parchment and similar material harder to ignite.
exceptions: Dampness can damage parchment.

spells.name: Dry

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Removes dampness and excess moisture from materials such as cloth and herbs.

spells.name: Dust

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Removes fine dust and tiny grit from exposed surfaces, transporting it elsewhere.
exceptions: Does not prevent new dust accumulating.

spells.name: Exterminate

fields.Area: One small pest, or up to ½ cubic foot of very tiny pests
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Kills a small pest such as a fly, mouse, rat or beetle.
Works on magical creations and ordinary creatures magically shrunk to insect size.
exceptions: Does not work on polymorphed creatures or similarly transformed beings.

spells.name: Flavor

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Changes or improves taste without changing the food’s quality or safety.
exceptions: Spoiled food stays spoiled and poison stays harmful; its warning taste may be concealed.

spells.name: Freshen

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Refreshes food, drink, flowers or herbs and removes slight spoilage.
Deals 1d4 damage to a creature harmed by purify food and drink.
conditions: Examples of size limits include a small cask, sheep or bushel.
exceptions: Less effective than purify food and drink; it is temporary.

spells.name: Gather

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Collects numerous small objects into a neat pile; can select one material type from a mixture.

spells.name: Polish

fields.Area: One object, such as a floor up to 1,000 square feet
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Smooths and gives luster to wood, metal, stone, leather or ceramic.
conditions: The surface must already be relatively clean; smaller objects generally polish better.

spells.name: Salt

fields.Area: One object, about 4 square yards or 30 gallons
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Sprinkles real salt onto the target; salt-vulnerable creatures take 1d4 damage.
conditions: Smaller targets can be oversalted; larger ones receive little salt.
exceptions: Underwater it produces about a pint of salt water that disperses unless contained.

spells.name: Shine

fields.Area: One object up to about 1 cubic yard
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Removes rust, tarnish and corrosion, making a suitable object mirror bright.
conditions: A previously devalued jewelry gem may be checked once more using the DMG p.26 value table with −1 on the roll.
exceptions: A gem cannot be revalued this way more than once.

spells.name: Spice

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates a real powdered or flaked spice/herb over food or drink, adding its substance rather than merely changing taste.

spells.name: Sprout

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Accelerates a small growth step: seeds sprout, sprouts gain about an inch, buds flower, and produce ripens.
exceptions: Can also push ripe fruit or vegetables into spoilage.

spells.name: Stitch

fields.Area: About 20 yards of cloth or 2 yards of leather
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Sews a new seam or repairs an old one in cloth or leather.
exceptions: The seam has ordinary strength.

spells.name: Sweeten

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates a real sweetener such as sugar, honey or syrup, following spice’s basic operation.

spells.name: Tie

fields.Area: One thread, string, cord, rope or cable
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes the object tie an ordinary knot of the chosen kind, to its own end or a similar object.
conditions: The ends to be joined must be within one foot of each other.

spells.name: Warm

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Raises a liquid’s or solid’s temperature by up to about 40°F.
exceptions: Cannot warm a living creature above its normal body temperature.

spells.name: Wrap

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates a suitable sturdy wrapping, such as tissue for powder, felt for gems or cloth for meal.
conditions: The wrapping opens normally or on the caster’s command.

spells.name: Curdle

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Curdles or accelerates spoilage/wilting of food and drink.
exceptions: Does not have the full effect of putrefy food and drink.

spells.name: Dirty

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Soils or stains surfaces, garments, dishes and similar objects; the opposite of clean.

spells.name: Dusty

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Coats exposed surfaces in a film of dust and grime.

spells.name: Hairy

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Lengthens and thickens hair, fur or similar growth by 2d6 inches; cutting removes it.
conditions: The reverse shortens or shaves growth.
exceptions: Reversing growth shorter than one inch prevents regrowth for 2d6 days.

spells.name: Knot

fields.Area: One thread, string, cord or rope
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Produces a difficult knot requiring 2d4 rounds to undo, reduced by the untyer’s Dexterity reaction bonus.
conditions: Can affect an existing tie cantrip.
exceptions: Cannot affect magical rope, a held rope or a taut line such as a bowstring.

spells.name: Ravel

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Unravels stitching if a thread is already loose/broken; magically stitched seams do not need an initial loose thread.
exceptions: Does not undo otherwise-magical items such as protective cloaks or bags of holding.

spells.name: Sour

fields.Area: One object; up to 1 pint of vinegar
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates real vinegar to sour food/drink or fill an empty container.

spells.name: Spill

fields.Area: One nonmagical container, about 1 gallon or smaller
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Tips a container so its solid or liquid contents spill.
exceptions: Securely closed/capped, larger or magical containers are unaffected.

spells.name: Tangle

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Entangles fine materials such as thread, hair and grass; ordinary untangling takes 3d4 rounds.
conditions: Rough removal can break or tear the material.
exceptions: Does not work on heavy rope.

spells.name: Tarnish

fields.Area: One object up to about 1 cubic yard
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Covers a susceptible surface with rust, corrosion, verdigris or similar tarnish.

spells.name: Untie

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Removes an ordinary tying or nullifies a tangle; on a difficult knot over a normal tying, it removes the difficult knot but leaves the normal tying.
exceptions: Has no effect on magical objects.

spells.name: Wilt

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes growing or picked vegetation wilt, droop or, if unhealthy, possibly wither.
exceptions: Applies only to vegetable material.

spells.name: Change

fields.Duration: Normally 1 turn; radical change 1 round, slight change 1+ days
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Changes a small object within the same animal or vegetable kingdom, with at most 50% change in size/volume.
conditions: Each transformation needs a separate casting; changing dead material to living is a radical, short-lived change.
exceptions: Small, normal, nonmagical animal-intelligence creatures get no save; other cases are not covered by that exemption.

spells.name: Distract

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes observers look to a location on the caster’s left or right, leaving another action unnoticed.
conditions: Only characters above level 0, or creatures with at least 1+1 HD and intelligence above low, receive saves.

spells.name: Hide

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes an object unseen by viewers in front of the caster, without concealing its sound.
conditions: Up to 2 cubic yards lasts one turn; each further 2 cubic yards through 20 reduces duration by one round, reaching one round at 20.
Above 20, each further 2 cubic yards removes one segment; 38 cubic yards lasts one segment, larger objects only momentarily disappear.
exceptions: Viewers beside or behind the caster are not affected; the caster may end it with the activating word.

spells.name: Mute

fields.Saving throw: A successful toucher’s spell save dispels it
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Temporarily reshapes or changes the material of a small glass, metal or stone object, such as a coin into a ring or copper into gold.
exceptions: Does not affect magical objects; touching can expose and end the change.

spells.name: Palm

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Conceals the real object under a hide-like effect while leaving a duplicate, allowing it to be secretly taken.
conditions: Unlike hide, viewer position does not matter.
exceptions: The duplicate must be screened before it vanishes after one segment or observers see it wink out.

spells.name: Present

fields.Area: Small item or several small objects
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Brings known, precisely located objects to the caster’s hand, up to a tankard-sized item or about a dozen coins.
conditions: Items on another person allow that person a spell save unless they are in plain sight.

spells.name: Belch

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Forces a belch; a failed save makes it very loud, while success makes it low and muffled.
exceptions: Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Blink

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes the subject blink; a successful save reduces this to one eye winking.
exceptions: A successful save gives a one-eyed creature no effect.
Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Cough

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Causes spasmodic coughing; a successful save produces only a brief hack, normally not interfering with other activities.
exceptions: Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Giggle

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Forces a chuckle/giggle; a successful save reduces it to a brief chuckle.
exceptions: Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Nod

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Causes a brief involuntary head nod, resembling agreement or greeting.
exceptions: Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Scratch

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Produces an itch and a roughly one-second involuntary scratch, after which the itch stops.
exceptions: Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Sneeze

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Causes one sneeze that relieves the induced nasal irritation.
exceptions: Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Twitch

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes a visible muscle twitch in a chosen appendage.
exceptions: Does not cause major discomfort or loss of control.
Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Wink

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes the subject wink: a failed save produces an exaggerated prolonged wink, success a rapid subtle one.
exceptions: Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Yawn

fields.Duration: Sleep vulnerability through the following round
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Forces a yawn and makes the subject more vulnerable to sleep through the rest of this round and the next.
For a group of multiple targets of 4 HD or fewer, one additional subject becomes vulnerable; two 4+1–4+4 HD creatures may be affected.
A victim up to 5+2 HD can be treated as 4+1–4+4 HD for sleep, with a 50% chance of not being affected.
exceptions: The same caster cannot cast this cantrip and a leveled spell in one round.
Does not break extreme concentration such as spellcasting (general person-affecting cantrip rule).

spells.name: Bee

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Summons an annoyed honey bee at a chosen spot within range; if it appears on a living creature, it is 90% likely to sting.

spells.name: Bluelight

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates a small blue light in the caster’s palm.
exceptions: It casts no reflections beyond its illumination radius and does not interfere with infravision or ultravision.

spells.name: Bug

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Summons an irritated beetle or similar bug at the chosen spot; it pinches, bites or otherwise attacks a creature on which it appears.

spells.name: Firefinger

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Produces a hot flame sufficient to ignite relatively dry parchment, twigs, kindling and similar material.

spells.name: Gnats

fields.Duration: 1d4 segments of distraction on failed save
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Summons gnats around the nearest living creature within 1″; failure to save distracts it before the swarm flies away.

spells.name: Mouse

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Summons a field mouse or similar species at a chosen point within range.
exceptions: The caster has no control over it; it reacts normally to the situation.

spells.name: Smokepuff

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates real white, gray, black, brown, yellow or green smoke at the chosen location.
exceptions: It rises or disperses under normal conditions; no fixed persistence is stated.

spells.name: Spider

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Summons an annoyed spider; an ordinary bite distracts for one segment.
There is a 5% chance of a strongly venomous species. Its victim saves versus poison at +4: success causes 1 hp; failure causes 2 hp and sickness preventing normal activity for 1d4 days.
exceptions: Neutralize poison removes the sickness; slow poison delays it one day.

spells.name: Tweak

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates an unseen pinch/pull on an ear, nose, cheek, beard, whiskers or tail.
conditions: Intelligence below 7 uses a spell save; at 7+, the source requires a 3d6 roll greater than Intelligence to avoid distraction.
exceptions: Harmless and annoying; it does not disrupt spellcasting.

spells.name: Unlock
