fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates a key-like force to open or close a basic prong, bolt-and-pin or bolt-and-spring lock.
exceptions: Tumblers, levers and secret combinations are beyond it; complex wards on an otherwise simple lock do not stop it.

spells.name: Creak

fields.Duration: Door: ⅓ segment; floorboards: ½ segment
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates the sound of rusty hinges opening or footsteps crossing squeaky boards; the latter can seem to travel up to 10 feet.

spells.name: Footfall

fields.Range: Begins within 1″; may move out to 2″
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates soft or noisy humanoid footsteps that approach, retreat, follow or parallel people.

spells.name: Groan

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates an illusory wracking cry heard by creatures that fail their spell saves.
exceptions: A door or container does not obstruct its range.

spells.name: Moan

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Uses groan’s operation for a pitiful high-pitched or eerie low-pitched moan.
exceptions: Doors and containers do not obstruct its range.

spells.name: Rattle

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates illusory rattling chains, with the same direction and distance limits as groan.

spells.name: Tap

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Makes one, two or three real taps against a solid object.
conditions: Able listeners within 1″ certainly hear it.

spells.name: Thump

fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates a loud muffled illusory impact as if a large object fell a short distance.

spells.name: Whistle

fields.Area: Audible at 10 feet faintly or 30 feet loudly
fields.Casting limit: Up to two cantrips/round; no leveled spell that round; second cantrip after 1d4 segments

effect: Creates a faint or loud whistle, either normal and sharp or hollow and eerie.

spells.name: Melt

fields.Area: 1 cubic yard of ice or 2 cubic yards of snow/level
fields.Materials: Rock-salt crystals and soot

effect: Turns the affected ice/snow to water; the listed volume melts in one round.
Against listed cold creatures such as white dragons, winter wolves, yeti or ice beings, deals 2 hp/caster level, or 1 hp/level on a successful spell save.
exceptions: Generally ineffective against other creature types.

spells.name: Mount

fields.Materials: Hair or dung of the animal type

effect: Summons a normal willing mount that returns home when the spell ends.
Listed mounts progress from mule/light horse (levels 1–3), draft horse/warhorse (4–7), camel (8–12), to elephant (13+; howdah at 18).
conditions: A lower-tier mount may be selected; riding gear is provided only when selecting below the caster’s available tier.
exceptions: Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Precipitation

fields.Materials: Silver dust; no holy symbol

effect: Produces the cleric spell’s light rain: dampens exposed materials and extinguishes small flames; large fires are largely unaffected.
conditions: Above 90°F duration doubles except in arid regions; near freezing it becomes sleet and at 30°F or lower snow.
exceptions: Large magical heat produces warm fog over double the area; magical cold freezes the water.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Taunt
effect: Makes failed savers charge the caster angrily and seek close combat rather than ranged attacks.
conditions: Only one creature type can be affected per casting, beginning with the nearest; Intelligence must be at least 2.
Strong leadership may grant +1 to +4 on saves at DM discretion.
exceptions: An impassable barrier such as a chasm or wall of flame breaks the effect.

spells.name: Wizard Mark

fields.Materials: Diamond dust worth about 50 gp and pigments; invisible marks also need a stylus

effect: Inscribe a personal rune and up to six smaller characters on stone, metal or softer surfaces without harming them.
conditions: Detect magic makes an invisible mark glow; invisibility/true-sight detection and specified seeing items also reveal it.
exceptions: Read magic reveals the intent; erase removes the mark.

spells.name: Bind
effect: Commands a nonliving rope-like object to coil, loop, tie/knot, or undo those actions.
Can serve as a trip line or entangle one opponent as the druid spell does.
conditions: Must be within about one foot of what it is to affect; a creature holding it overrides the spell.
Thicker material proportionally reduces length; halving diameter increases length by 50%.
exceptions: Cannot garrote or gain other magical-rope powers; 2 slashing damage breaks it.
No separate material component is identified beyond the rope-like subject.

spells.name: Deeppockets

fields.Materials: High-quality robe/gown, golden needle and twisted cloth strip

effect: Enchants a garment worth at least 300 gp with at least 12 pockets: one pocket holds 1,000 gp weight and 5 cubic feet as only 100 gp weight, without a bulge.
Alternatively use ten pockets each holding 100 gp weight and ½ cubic foot. A garment with at least 100 pockets costs at least 1,000 gp and permits 100 pockets of 10 gp weight and ⅙ cubic foot each.
conditions: On expiry or dispelling, the wearer saves versus spell: success spills contents around them; failure loses them into astral space.

spells.name: Irritation

fields.Materials: Powdered poison ivy, oak or sumac leaf

effect: Itching: spending 5–8 segments scratching avoids three subsequent rounds of squirming and a −2 attack penalty; spells are ruined in the initial round.
Rash: begins after 1d4 rounds, lowers Comeliness by 1/day for up to four days (maximum four-point loss), then Dexterity by 1 after a week; cure disease or dispel magic removes it and restores scores.
exceptions: Thick/insensitive skins are essentially unaffected.
The itching paragraph says AC is 'lowered' by 4; numeric direction is not resolved here.

spells.name: Know Alignment
effect: Reads exact alignment using the cleric spell’s basic effect; observing for only one round reveals law/chaos alone.
exceptions: The reverse uses the cleric spell’s alignment-concealment principle; no separate allocation procedure is supplied in UA.

spells.name: Preserve

fields.Materials: Dust, resin/amber and brandy

effect: Keeps material fresh and intact for later spell use.
Caster levels 2–4 can preserve hard/dry material, 5–7 soft/wet material, and 8+ semiliquids/liquids.
conditions: Moist materials require a container.
exceptions: Does not preserve periodically gathered items such as mistletoe/holly potency, or preserve a corpse for resurrection.

spells.name: Vocalize

fields.Materials: Clapperless bell or jailbird’s tongue

effect: Allows spells requiring verbal components to be cast silently, provided their entire casting finishes within vocalize’s duration.
exceptions: Does not remove silence or restore other communication; audible spell effects remain masked while silence persists.

spells.name: Whip

fields.Materials: Miniature braided silk whip

effect: Cracking the whip keeps ordinary animals at bay unless they save versus spell; an animal actually struck makes a separate spell save at −1 to −4 or retreats for at least an hour, without damage.
A weapon-wrapping hit disarms only if the whip saves (13+ against an edge, 6+ otherwise) and the victim fails a spell save; recovering the weapon takes a round.
conditions: Animal effect excludes Intelligence above 3, monsters and giant animals larger than bears.
Weapon magic penalizes the whip’s item save; target magic resistance must first fail.

spells.name: Zephyr

fields.Area: 1″ path, ½″ per caster level in length
fields.Materials: Accordion-folded fine parchment and a pin

effect: Fans larger fires for +1 per damage die; holds moving vapor such as cloudkill back for one round.
Halves fog cloud/wall of fog duration, or pushes stagnant air/gas back 1″ and halves its duration/potency unless replenished.
exceptions: The printed pin-material wording is ambiguous.

spells.name: Cloudburst

fields.Materials: Powdered silver and iodine crystals; no holy symbol

effect: Uses the cleric spell’s downpour: drenches within one segment; small/medium/large normal fires go out immediately/in 3–5/in 8–10 segments.
Large magical fires produce steam over four times the area for 1d3 damage/round, doubled against cold-dwellers/users.
conditions: Steam normally persists 2–5 rounds, shortened by wind; permanent magical fires relight in 1–2 rounds.
exceptions: Arid climate reduces it to double precipitation, hot humidity extends it to two rounds, and freezing changes it to sleet/snow.
Cannot be used underwater (UA p.81).

spells.name: Detect Illusion

fields.Area: Line of sight 1″ wide and 1″/level long
fields.Materials: Yellow-tinted crystal, glass or mica

effect: Recognizes an illusion as unreal.
conditions: Can let another creature see it as unreal while the caster touches that viewer with both hands and the viewer looks at the illusion.

spells.name: Item
effect: Shrinks an ordinary nonmagical subject to one-twelfth size, optionally making it cloth-like.
Throwing an affected object onto a solid surface or the original caster’s command restores its normal size/material.
conditions: Fire and its fuel can be affected.
exceptions: Subsequent item saves use the original material, even when transformed to cloth.
No separate material component is specified in the paragraph.

spells.name: Material
effect: Creates basic raw material such as stone, soil, wood, water, air, straw or dung.
conditions: For simple plants, failure chance is 100% minus 1% per caster level.
exceptions: Cannot create animal life, worked/refined products, tough gems or precious metals.

spells.name: Secret Page

fields.Materials: Powdered herring scales

effect: Disguises a page’s contents as different writing; the caster’s command reveals/reconceals it, while repeating the command twice removes the spell.
conditions: Confuse languages or explosive runes can be added.
exceptions: Comprehend languages does not reveal it; a failed dispel magic destroys the page.
Will-o-wisp or boggart essence, alter reality or wish can reveal the true nature.

spells.name: Sepia Snake Sigil

fields.Materials: Amber powder worth 100 gp, snake scale and mushroom spores

effect: A snake-like force attacks the nearest living creature other than the caster as a monster of caster-level HD.
A hit traps the victim in immovable amber force: no aging, hunger, sleep, spell recovery or outside awareness until the caster releases it or dispel magic works.
conditions: Can be an aimed airborne sigil, a surface glyph triggered by touch/gaze, or a character protecting magical writing.
exceptions: Nothing reaches or moves the trapped victim; a miss dissipates with flash/noise and a one-round smoke puff.

spells.name: Wind Wall

fields.Area: 1″ wide and ½″ high per caster level
fields.Materials: Tiny fan and exotic feather

effect: Creates an invisible updraft that lifts birds as large as crows and loose material; ordinary insects cannot cross.
conditions: A spell save may determine whether someone keeps hold of papers or similar objects.
exceptions: Cannot function underwater except within airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Dispel Illusion
effect: Dispels a non-illusionist’s phantasmal force automatically under the base rule.
Against another illusionist’s illusion/phantasm, use effective caster level two below actual: base chance 50%, −2% per level lower or +5% per level higher than the original caster.

spells.name: Magic Mirror

fields.Materials: Silver mirror worth at least 1,000 gp; hawk/eagle/roc eye, nitric acid, copper and zinc

effect: Makes a crystal-ball-like scrying mirror. Comprehend languages, read magic, tongues, infravision and ultravision work through it.
Detect magic, detect good/evil, message and detect illusion work with a 5% chance/caster level.
conditions: The mirror survives, unlike the other material components.
exceptions: Targets can detect scrying under crystal-ball rules; cavaliers have a base 5% chance and barbarians 1%, as noted here.

spells.name: Shout

fields.Materials: Honey, citric acid and a bull/ram horn cone

effect: Deafens creatures in the cone for 2–12 rounds and deals 2–12 damage on a failed save; exposed brittle/sonic-vulnerable material shatters.
conditions: Use is limited to once a day to avoid risking permanent deafness to the caster.
exceptions: Cannot function underwater except within airy water (UA p.81).

spells.name: Ultravision

fields.Materials: Crushed amethyst worth at least 500 gp

effect: Gives clear night vision to 100 yards and indistinct vision to about 300; very dark clouds halve its reach.
conditions: More than 6 feet of earth or 3 feet of stone blocks sky radiation, leaving dim vision within about 3 feet unless another emission source exists.
exceptions: Nearby bright light, including magical light, spoils distant ultraviolet perception.

spells.name: Avoidance

fields.Materials: Magnetized needle

effect: Creates repulsion between an object and living things, maintaining about one foot of separation; relative mass determines which moves.
The reverse, attraction, makes smaller creatures move toward the object or the object slide toward a larger creature.
conditions: Applying it to worn/carried property allows the carrier a save.
exceptions: Cannot be cast directly on living things; freeing something adhered by attraction requires a successful bend-bars roll.

spells.name: Dismissal

fields.Materials: Material repugnant to target; reverse uses pleasing material

effect: Attempts to send a known type/named extraplanar creature home, after magic resistance; caster/target level or HD difference modifies its spell save.
The reverse, beckon, brings a similarly identified creature to the caster’s plane; a known proper name bypasses the reverse’s magic-resistance check.
conditions: For dismissal, the caster must be on the Prime Material Plane.
The creature’s type must be known; any given name, proper name or surname it has must also be known and used in the spell.
A willing dismissal target uses an unmodified save.
exceptions: Successful dismissal has a 20% chance of sending it to the wrong plane.
Beckoning neither controls it nor assures friendliness; Prime-native or partly Prime-ancestry creatures are excluded.

spells.name: Dolor
effect: Produces increasing unease that penalizes saves against commands and nonoffensive magic by −1, then −2, then −3 across the described stages.
conditions: The verbal component must concern the creature’s class and include as much information about the subject as possible.
exceptions: A higher-Intelligence subject has a 5%-per-point advantage chance to charm/dominate the caster; interruption during casting makes that domination automatic.

spells.name: Leomund’s Lamentable Belabourment
effect: Engages failed savers in consuming conversation. After three rounds, repeated saves in rounds 4–6 can lead to 3d4 rounds of wandering confusion.
After six rounds, another failed save causes 2–5 rounds of rage against other subjects or oneself; successful savers instead collapse lamenting for 1d4 rounds unless disturbed.
conditions: Subjects must understand the language; Intelligence ≤2 is immune. Save modifiers: Int 3–7 −1, 8–10 none, 11–14 +1, 15+ +2.
Unattacked subjects ignore other events; if the caster leaves they continue one more round without further continuation checks.

spells.name: Sending

fields.Materials: Two open-ended tiny cylinders connected by copper wire

effect: Sends one word/caster level, not counting articles, to a creature whose name and appearance the caster knows well.
A recipient with Intelligence as low as 1 understands it.
conditions: Failure chance is 5% per plane separating caster and recipient.
exceptions: The recipient is not compelled to act.

spells.name: Ensnarement

fields.Materials: A prepared protective circle, thaumaturgic triangle, or pentagram; optional special pigments or permanent inlay as described.

effect: Lures a named extraplanar creature through an apparent planar opening, intending to confine it until it agrees to one service.

The creature detects the trap on a 3d6 roll at or below its intelligence. Subtract its intelligence advantage over the caster from the roll, or add the caster's advantage. A successful check makes it ignore the opening.
A captive that agrees to serve returns instantly to its original plane when the single service is complete and it informs the caster.
conditions: State the creature's type, and its proper or given name if it has one.

Ensnarement itself does not prevent the captive from harming the caster. Use a magic circle for upper-plane or Astral creatures, a thaumaturgic triangle for Ethereal, Elemental, or Concordant Opposition creatures, or a pentagram for lower or infernal creatures.

A hand-drawn protection has a 20% base escape chance. An inlaid or carved design has a 10% base chance, tested only initially to establish whether it was made properly. Modify the chance by the difference between caster intelligence plus experience level and captive intelligence plus level or hit dice: subtract a caster advantage, add a captive advantage.

Special pigments costing 1,000 gp per turn of preparation reduce a hand-made design's base chance by 1% per turn, to zero before the intelligence/level adjustment. Improving a permanent design to zero base chance takes at least one full month and at least 50,000 gp beyond its ordinary cost.

The DM rates a bribe, promise, or threat from 0 to 6 and subtracts that rating from the captive's intelligence. A roll at or below its adjusted intelligence refuses service. Offers can be renewed after 24 hours; confinement reduces intelligence by 1 for each such day.
exceptions: Any break or blur in the protective inscription releases the captive automatically; even a straw crossing a line ruins it. The captive cannot itself place an object across the magical barrier.
Impossible or unreasonable commands are never accepted. A released creature may seek revenge.

spells.name: Eyebite
effect: Meet the subject's gaze and speak one word to apply one of four effects. Choosing any one effect expends the spell.
Charm makes a person or monster utterly loyal and docile toward the caster, even in personal danger; other rules follow charm person or charm monster. A spell save negates it.
Fear acts as the fear spell unless the subject saves versus spell.

Sicken halves the subject's normal ability scores and movement; it must rest for half of each turn to move at all. A failed spell save also causes loss of 1 actual constitution point per day until death at zero.
Sleep causes a comatose slumber unless the subject saves versus spell. Shaking or another shock awakens an affected creature.
conditions: Sicken affects creatures with ability scores. Nonhuman, nondemi-human, nonhumanoid creatures receive +4 on their save against sicken.
Dispel magic, heal, alter reality, limited wish, or wish removes sicken.
Subjects normally affected by the 1st-level sleep spell save at −2 against the sleep option.
exceptions: Cure disease does not remove sicken. Creatures without ability scores are unaffected by that option.
Undead are immune to the sleep option.

spells.name: Mordenkainen’s Lucubration
effect: Restores one previously memorized and cast 1st- through 5th-level spell used within the preceding 24 hours, as though it had not been cast.
The recalled spell can be cast normally on a later round.
conditions: The selected spell must actually have been memorized and used within the stated period.
Any material components required by the recalled spell must be available before it can be used.
exceptions: Recalls only one spell per casting and cannot restore a spell above 5th level.

spells.name: Transmute Water to Dust

fields.Area: 1 cubic spell-inch per caster level; muddy water doubles this, wet mud quadruples it
fields.Materials: Diamond dust worth at least 500 gp and a bit of seashell. The reverse additionally requires a pinch of ordinary dust. The magic-user does not require mistletoe.

effect: Changes water in the selected area into powdery dust. Only liquid present when the spell is cast is affected.
Other water that contacts the dust can soak it or turn it into silty mud. Water within mixed liquids is affected, and water-containing potions are ruined.
The reverse produces water on the corresponding large scale.
Underwater, the spell opens a hole of 10 cubic feet per caster level. If enough water surrounds it, the inrush deals 1–4 damage per caster level to everyone within, without a save.
conditions: The magic-user version follows the druid spell with the magic-user header and no mistletoe.
One creature native to the Elemental Plane of Water can be affected per casting, regardless of its size or the spell's area; it receives a spell save to escape the effect.
exceptions: Ordinary living creatures are unaffected.
The underwater modification is expressly extended to the magic-user version on printed page 82.

spells.name: Banishment

fields.Saving throw: Special; spell save and magic resistance
fields.Area: Up to 2 creature levels or hit dice per caster level
fields.Materials: Substances harmful, hateful, or opposed to the subject's nature; the choice determines saving-throw penalties.

effect: Instantly returns extraplanar subjects to their own plane. They require a special summoning or another means of egress to return.
Each ordinary appropriate material imposes a −2 penalty on the subject's spell save. Especially potent materials may count as −3 or −4; less apt ones may count as only −1.
A subject that saves causes an energy backlash dealing 2–12 points of damage and stunning the caster for 2–12 segments.
conditions: All intended subjects must be within range and within the total level/hit-die allowance.
The caster must state the type and true proper name of the subject and invoke powers opposed to it. Its magic resistance must be overcome.
Actively opposed powers or powers actively favorable to the caster can further improve component efficacy by −1 through −6, at the referee's discretion.

spells.name: Forcecage

fields.Area: A cube 2″ on each side; forcecube variant is 1″ on each side
fields.Materials: At memorization, powder a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp and trace the intended cage or cube with its dust; toss the dust away to complete the study. No material is used in the later casting.

effect: Forms a cage of alternating bands of force with open gaps. Creatures that cannot pass through the gaps are confined.
Spells and breath weapons pass through the gaps.
Special preparation at memorization instead produces forcecube, with one-eighth the cage's volume; it follows the cube of force device's effects except for differences inherent in a cast spell.
conditions: A creature with magic resistance gets one attempt to pass the force walls using that resistance. Each other creature must qualify separately.
The cage ends by dispel magic or when its duration expires.
Printed page 81 lists forcecage among the effects that a separate permanency spell can make lasting.
exceptions: The cage consists of alternating force bands with ½-foot gaps.
The forcecube variant imports the cube of force device rules; consult that device for its detailed barrier effects.

spells.name: Mordenkainen’s Magnificent Mansion

fields.Materials: A miniature ivory portal, a small piece of polished marble, and a tiny silver spoon; all are destroyed.

effect: Creates a furnished extradimensional dwelling reached through one portal on the casting plane. The visible entrance is a faint shimmer about 4 ft. wide and 8 ft. high.
The caster controls entry, closes and conceals the portal upon entering, and may reopen it from inside.
Provides obedient translucent servants and a nine-course banquet for as many dozens of guests as the caster has experience levels.
The interior is clean, fresh, and warm; rest works normally, and conditions do not cross between the mansion and the outside.
Underwater, the caster may choose a water-filled mansion or keep the interior dry by excluding water.
conditions: Food sustains guests only while inside. After leaving, replace each imaginary meal with one hour spent eating ordinary food.
For each unreplaced imaginary meal, lose 1 strength point. Eating as specified restores the points if done within 6 hours; otherwise the loss becomes permanent.
The text suggests that the interior design can be altered to suit the caster.
exceptions: Access is through the special portal only. Mansion food's nourishment ends immediately outside, causing ravenous hunger.

spells.name: Sequester

fields.Materials: Basilisk eyelash, gum arabic, and a dram of whitewash.

effect: Conceals affected objects or creatures from detection and location spells and makes them invisible to normal forms of sight or seeing.
Living and undead subjects become comatose in suspended animation until the effect expires or is dispelled.
conditions: An unwilling creature able to resist and avoid the spell receives its normal spell save.
exceptions: Touch can still discover a subject.
Devices such as a robe of eyes or gem of seeing can still reveal the concealed subject.

spells.name: Teleport Without Error

fields.Area: Special; caster and the load allowed by teleport
fields.Load: Maximum 2,500 gp weight + 1,500 gp weight per caster level above 10 (PHB p.82)
fields.Base rule: Teleport, PHB p.82; off-plane destinations use the table below.
fields.Off-plane error table: Studied carefully: high 01–04, on target 05–98, low 99–00; seen casually: 01–08, 09–96, 97–00; viewed once: 01–16, 17–92, 93–00; never seen: 01–32, 33–84, 85–00. Extraplanar knowledge is at best studied carefully.

effect: Transports the caster and the normal teleport load to a known location on the caster's home plane without error.
Can also reach another plane, using teleport's error table and the caster's actual knowledge of the destination.
conditions: An extraplanar destination can be no better than 'Studied carefully', and that rating requires the caster to have visited and carefully surveyed the area.
The caster can take no other action during the round of arrival.
Succor supplies a separately described exception to the normal extraplanar travel risk.
exceptions: Extraplanar transport retains a chance of error; the guaranteed accuracy applies to known home-plane locations.
The inherited teleport load allowance and planar error table are not reproduced in this UA description.

spells.name: Torment

fields.Saving throw: Special; magic resistance and progressive spell saves
fields.Materials: A specially written scroll naming the creature's type by its secret name or naming the individual, and identifying the caster. Special inks cost at least 1,000 gp per subject hit die.

effect: Forces a captive extraplanar creature toward accepting a demanded service through increasingly painful recitation.
After the initial link, continued reading causes twinges in rounds 1–2, shooting pains in rounds 3–4, then aches and cramps in rounds 5–6.
The subject's spell-save penalties are −1, −2, −3, −4, −6, and −8 in rounds 1 through 6 respectively. Failure means agreement to the demand.

If it escapes, the subject suffers −1 initiative per two rounds of torment, to a maximum −4 at round 8. Its attack and per-die damage penalties begin at −1 after round 3, rise to −4 in round 6, then recede to −1 in round 9.
conditions: The subject must be confined in a magic circle, thaumaturgic triangle, or pentagram, and applicable magic resistance must fail.
For each intelligence point the creature has above the caster, it has a 1% chance of seizing control, pulling the caster into the prison, and carrying the caster to its own plane.
If the reading is interrupted or distracted, its chance to seize control is 5% per intelligence point.
An agreement is obeyed literally; the subject remains intensely hostile and seeks revenge.
exceptions: The source explicitly removes a penalty after round 8 but supplies no legible save-penalty values for rounds 7–8 in this passage; no values have been extrapolated.
Compare ensnarement and dolor for related confinement and coercion rules.

spells.name: Truename

fields.Casting time: Special; initial name/history recitation takes 3 segments
fields.Polymorph verse counts: Mineral to animal 10; mineral to vegetable 9; vegetable to animal 8; monster to normal 7; monster to monster 6; other to human 5; animal to animal 4; vegetable to vegetable 3; mineral to mineral 2. Reverses use the same count; use the closest stated case for others.
fields.Transport verse counts: Same plane: 100 miles 4; 500 miles 5; 2,000 miles 6. One plane/world removed: 7; two removed: 8.

effect: Invokes a living thing's secret true name, followed by verse about its nature or history, to produce one of several commands or transformations.
Multiple suggestion permits 1–4 suggestion effects, each taking one further segment of verse.

Weakness and surrender removes 1 strength point per segment, with −1 to hit, damage, and movement rate for each point lost; each loss requires a save versus paralyzation or surrender. Strength and the will to resist return 2–8 rounds after recitation ends.

Polymorph works as polymorph any object without system shock. The subject retains original hit points but thinks and behaves like its assumed kind; duration is 6 turns per caster level minus 1 turn per required transformation verse.
Transport moves the subject without error; it automatically gains the physical adaptations needed to survive normal destination conditions.
conditions: The caster must know the actual true name, which common names usually are not. Discovering it can require research, spying, legend lore, or difficult sagecraft.
After the opening 3 segments, continue in verse to describe the desired result.
Transport of willing subjects permits no save, even for subjects with magic resistance.
Interruption during recitation ruins and expends the spell.

spells.name: Volley

fields.Materials: Flexible bent willow or similar wood, crisscrossed with specially prepared gut strands.

effect: Reflects an incoming spell upon its caster. If the originator saves versus spell, it returns toward the volley caster, who must then save; it continues until a save fails or its power expires.
Reflects the whole spell, so an area attack can leave other members of the volley caster's party unharmed.

Each return takes one second. An incoming spell lasts for a number of complete exchanges equal to its spell level, with each individual reflection counting as half an exchange; the original casting is not counted.
conditions: Volley must already have been cast to receive the attack.
Range, duration, area, and resulting effects depend on the incoming spell and circumstances.

spells.name: Binding

fields.Saving throw: Special; see caster level and form
fields.Materials: Chanted text and gestures; materials vary, including appropriate miniature metal chains, rare soporific herbs, a diamond or corundum worth 1,000 gp per subject hit die, and a vellum likeness or carved statuette.

effect: Imprisons a lower-planar creature already held inside a restraining diagram. Choose one of six forms.
Chaining confines it with restraints that produce antipathy toward approaching creatures other than the caster; it lasts up to one year per effective caster level.
Slumber produces coma for up to one year per effective caster level. Bound slumber combines coma and chaining for up to one month per effective caster level.
Hedged prison confines it within an area until the magical hedge is broken. Metamorphosis makes all but its face or head noncorporeal until a prescribed freeing act.
Minimus containment reduces it to an inch tall or smaller and confines it within a gem or comparable prison. The last three forms radiate only a very faint magic aura.
conditions: No save applies if effective caster level is at least twice the subject's hit dice. Otherwise it receives a modified spell save; success frees it.
At most six magic-users can assist. Each assistant of 9th level or above adds one-third of that assistant's level; each assistant of levels 4–8 adds one level.
Chaining uses the ordinary save; slumber grants +1, bound slumber +2, hedged prison +3, metamorphosis +4, minimus containment +5.
Prior dolor imposes −1, prior torment −2, and the two used successively −4 on the save.

The first three forms can be renewed. After one year the captive gains a normal spell save and breaks free on success; interference that weakens chaining or slumber can also permit a normal save on renewal.
exceptions: The first three forms keep the subject within its restraining diagram.
Where the source says relative caster-level/hit-die ratio modifies an allowed save, it supplies no additional numeric ratio formula in this passage.

spells.name: Demand

fields.Saving throw: Special; spell save against the suggestion
fields.Materials: Two cylinders open at one end, connected by thin copper wire, plus a small part of the subject, such as hair or nail.
fields.Message limit: One word/caster level, excluding articles; Sending, UA p.59

effect: Works as sending, but the message can include a suggestion. A subject failing its spell save tries to carry that suggestion out.
conditions: If circumstances make the requested action relatively impossible or incongruous, the recipient understands the message but makes no save and the suggestion has no effect.
As sending, requires a familiar creature whose name and appearance are well known.
As sending, delivery failure chance is 5% per intervening plane; a subject of Intelligence 1 can understand.
exceptions: The sending spell supplies the underlying message and delivery rules; this UA passage does not repeat them.

spells.name: Otiluke’s Telekinetic Sphere

fields.Area: Sphere 1 ft. in diameter per caster level
fields.Materials: A hemisphere of diamond or similar hard clear gem, a matching gum-arabic hemisphere, and two small bar magnets.

effect: Encloses a creature that fits inside a shimmering force globe unless it saves versus spell, as Otiluke's resilient sphere; the contents weigh one-sixteenth normal.
The caster can telekinetically lift a sphere containing a subject whose actual weight is up to 5,000 lb.; after enclosure, control extends to 1″ per caster level.
A heavier load still weighs only one-sixteenth normal and can therefore be rolled without exceptional effort.
Movement and falls while enclosed are relatively harmless to the contents because of their reduced effective weight.
Nothing passes through the barrier, inward or outward, but the subject breathes normally. It can be moved physically, including by struggles from inside.
conditions: The sphere is immune to damage except from a rod of cancellation, a wand of negation, disintegrate, or dispel magic. These destroy the globe without harming its contents.
exceptions: A sphere expiring while aloft can leave the subject falling onto a hard surface.

spells.name: Sink

fields.Area: One creature, or one object of up to 1 cubic spell-inch per caster level

effect: After four uninterrupted segments, a failed save roots the subject in place and gives it the density of the supporting surface.
The caster may stop then: the rooting expires after four turns. Continuing sinks the subject by one-quarter of its height in each of segments 5–8, until completely buried.
A sunken living subject is held unharmed in a state like stasis. Its uppermost part lies as far beneath the surface as the subject is tall.
Removing the surrounding ground breaks the spell and restores the subject, but does not raise it.
Underwater, it sinks below the river or sea floor; the containment's magic aura radiates through the water to the surface.
conditions: Creatures save versus spell. Magical objects save versus disintegration; items of magical origin, enchanted items, and protected items qualify. Nonmagical objects receive no save.
Dig, transmute rock to mud, and freedom can aid recovery without harming the subject.

Detect magic over the site reveals a faint, unclassifiable dweomer even when the buried subject is beyond detection range. If the subject is in range, its enchantment-alteration character is discernible.

spells.name: Crystalbrittle
effect: Changes one metal item, including adamantite or an iron golem, into extremely fragile crystalline material.
An affected item struck by an ordinary metal tool or a weighty weapon, including a staff, shatters and is permanently destroyed.
conditions: Touching worn or wielded equipment, or a monster, requires a successful combat hit.
Magic items save according to their magical bonus value or protection. The printed examples are a +1/+3 sword 10% (average the pluses), +5 armor 25%, and an iron golem 15%.
Metal artifacts and relics have a 95% chance to resist.
exceptions: Only a single item is affected; changing armor does not also change its wearer's shield.
Dispel magic cannot restore the metal; a wish is required.

spells.name: Energy Drain

fields.Materials: Essence of spectre or vampire dust.

effect: Makes the caster a conduit to the Negative Material Plane. Touching a living victim and speaking the trigger word drains two energy levels.
A monster permanently loses two hit dice for hit points and attacks. A character loses the associated levels, hit dice, hit points, and abilities, recoverable through advancement where applicable.
Humans or humanoids reduced to zero energy level become juju zombies.
conditions: The three-segment preparation is followed by casting forth the material; a combat victim must then be hit by touch.
Every use has a 5% chance to drain one energy level from the caster as well.

spells.name: Mordenkainen’s Disjunction
effect: Disjoins magic and magic items in the radius: spells are broken into components, usually spoiling them as dispel magic would, and magic items can become mundane.
Items or magic actually cast upon a creature save versus spell; otherwise the source calls for a save versus dispel magic.
Artifacts and relics can be affected, with a chance of 1% per caster level.
conditions: Magic on the caster's person, and anything the caster is touching, is excluded.
If an artifact is destroyed, the caster must save versus spell at −4 or permanently lose all spellcasting ability.
Destroying an artifact has a 95% chance to attract a powerful being interested in or connected with it.
exceptions: The source applies the effect broadly to potions, scrolls, rings, rods, miscellaneous magic, artifacts and relics, magic armor, and weapons.
The unusual 'versus dispel magic' save instruction is retained as printed rather than converted to a later edition's saving system.

spells.name: Succor

fields.Materials: An object made of gem material worth at least 5,000 gp, faceted or otherwise; it may be enchanted only once per month, usually on a clear full-moon night.

effect: Enchants an object that is willingly given to one individual along with a command word. Breaking it while speaking the word teleports the holder and carried or worn possessions without error to the selected destination.
The reversed use instead brings the archmage to the holder's immediate vicinity. This magic-user version compels the archmage to answer.
When the object is enchanted, fix its use and destination: the casting location or a place well known to the magic-user.
conditions: Each intervening plane adds a cumulative 1% chance of irrevocable loss of the traveler or summoned caster.
The inherited cleric description limits the effect to the individual; no additional creatures are transported.
exceptions: The cleric version allows its caster to refuse a reverse summons; this magic-user version expressly removes that option.
The MU material value and preparation time override the cleric spell's lesser requirements.
